value.body: Studies the soil and rock at a site — through boreholes, field tests and lab tests — and uses the results to design foundations, retaining walls, slopes and earthworks. Employers include geotechnical consultancies, soil-investigation firms, infrastructure contractors and public agencies building roads, railways, dams and metro lines. Work splits between field investigation, lab testing and design calculations and reports.

items.label: Typical entry
items.note: An M.Tech in Geotechnical Engineering is common for design roles

items.label: Key tests
items.value: SPT, plate load test, triaxial and consolidation tests

items.label: National highways built in a year
items.note: Foundations, embankments and slopes on such projects need soil investigation
items.source: Ministry of Road Transport & Highways (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers often start at a soil-investigation firm or as site engineers on foundation-heavy projects, logging boreholes and supervising tests. Design roles at consultancies usually prefer an M.Tech in Geotechnical Engineering, with admission mainly through GATE. GATE scores also open public-sector posts that involve geotechnical work.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Field and lab testing of soil and rock
Foundation design — shallow, pile and raft

value.title: At a glance
items: A specialist field: fewer openings than general civil roles, with demand tied to infrastructure projects.
Fieldwork, often at remote sites, is part of the early years.
Next roles: senior geotechnical engineer, foundation design lead, or work in tunnelling and ground improvement.
